sources.citation: Westrum, Peter N. and Susan Westrum. 1975. A preliminary Berik phonology. Irian: Bulletin of Irian Jaya Development 4(1): 1-41.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Not Bonerif, but the only phonology of any Tor-family language (Berik, Bonerif's closest relative per Usher); would supply the family-level stress pattern if a proxy is ever wanted.
sources.venue: Irian: Bulletin of Irian Jaya Development

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World: 'Bonerif' page (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch), Tor River > Berik-Bonerif.
sources.note: Phonology section '[under construction]' and empty; sources listed are wordlists only (Oosterwal 1961:274-277, Voorhoeve 1975:107 after Anceaux, Smits & Voorhoeve 1994:18-266 after Oosterwal).

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World: 'Edwas' page (= Beneraf/Nengke villages, the ISO bnv identity since 2008).
sources.note: Phonology '[under construction]'; only source Lee & Wambaliau 2004:49-62 (239-item wordlists, 21 sentences); pronoun forms reproduced with phonetic stress marks (e.g. 'in-teu, 'de-teu, ne-'teu) but no rule stated.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. Change Request 2007-212 (R. Lebold, SIL), adopted 2008-01-14: bnv reference name Bonerif -> Beneraf, additional names Bonerif, Edwas.
sources.note: Nothing; identity evidence only (SIL rapid appraisal survey Aug 2005; cites draft 'Survey Report on the Kwanem Languages').

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 2007. Australasia and the Pacific. In Christopher Moseley (ed.), Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages, 425-577. London: Routledge. Entry 'Bonerif [150]' p. 480 (cross-referenced by the Foya, Itik, Keder, Mander, Maremgi, Sause entries for Tor structural notes).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Family-level structural remark only: 'Structurally the Tor languages correspond to the TNGP type, but have rudimentary gender distinction in verb forms, and directional markers. There is number marking in nouns.' The generic 'TNGP type' note (Damal entry) says 'presence of phonologically relevant tones in many of them' for the phylum as a whole, not attributed to Tor or Bonerif. Nothing on Bonerif stress, accent or tone.
sources.venue: Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew, Robert Attenborough, Jack Golson & Robin Hide (eds.). 2005. Papuan Pasts: cultural, linguistic and biological histories of Papuan-speaking peoples. Pacific Linguistics 572. Canberra: ANU. (Chapters touching the Tor area: Ross, M. 'Pronouns as a preliminary diagnostic for grouping Papuan languages', 15-65; Donohue, M. & M. Crowther 'Meeting in the middle: interaction in North-Central New Guinea', 167-184; Roscoe, P. 'Foraging, ethnographic analogy, and Papuan pasts', 555-584.)
sources.note: Bonerif appears only as a row in Roscoe's contact-era territory/settlement tables (terrestrial foragers; data from Oosterwal 1961) and implicitly in Ross's family list; Donohue & Crowther's tables mention 'Tor River / Tor' and 'Orya' for coastal-contact history. No phonology; a full-text search for stress/accent/tone near Tor/Orya/Sarmi = 0.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Bibliography to 1995: only indexes, checklist, atlas. No descriptive or phonological work on this language is indexed.

sources.citation: Greenhill, S. TransNewGuinea.org, language 'Beneraf' (bone1255): 37 lexical items from Voorhoeve 1975.

Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 345-460. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU. Section 2.6.2.2.11.1 'The Tor-Lake Plain Stock', 2.6.2.2.11.1.5 'The Tor Family', pp. 413-414.
sources.note: Named as a Tor Family member ('Bonerif is spoken on an eastern tributary of the middle Tor River'); pronoun chart; no phonology.
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists (Pacific Linguistics B-31). Canberra: ANU. Bonerif = entry 74 pp. 38-39; wordlist 74 p. 107 (after Anceaux); transcription conventions p. 92.
sources.note: Nothing language-specific; the wordlist conventions state (p. 92) 'Stress and pitch are not indicated.' Bonerif entry gives only village (Urbefare), population and sources (Oosterwal 1961; Voorhoeve 1971).
sources.venue: Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists (Pacific Linguistics B-31)

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 47-114. Tor Stock section 2.3.5.1, pp. 66-67ff.
sources.note: Nothing; Bonerif (BO) appears only as forms in lexicostatistic cognate sets taken from Oosterwal 1961; no phonology of any Tor language.
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28)

sources.citation: Oosterwal, Gottfried. 1961. People of the Tor: A cultural-anthropological study on the tribes of the Tor territory (Northern Netherlands New-Guinea). Assen: Van Gorcum (PhD Utrecht). Wordlists pp. 274-277.
sources.note: Original inland Bonerif (Urbefare) wordlist; a note on spelling/pronunciation may accompany the lists. archive.org has two lending-restricted scans (bwb_Y0-EAG-399, bwb_p9-dzj-070).

sources.citation: Lee, Sang-Kem and Theresia Wambaliau. 2004. Kwanem languages survey report in Northeastern Papua, Indonesia. Unpublished SIL (Papua) survey report, 88 pp. ('to appear in SIL Electronic Survey Reports'; cited as draft in ISO 639-3 CR 2007-212).

sources.citation: Smits, Leo and C. L. Voorhoeve (eds.). 1994. The J. C. Anceaux collection of wordlists of Irian Jaya languages, B: Non-Austronesian (Papuan) languages, Part I. Irian Jaya Source Materials No. 9, Series B No. 3. Leiden/Jakarta: DSALCUL/IRIS. Bonerif/Beneraf pp. 18-266.
